Seleucus I Nicator: Macedonian general, Diadochus, and founder of the Seleucid Empire.

Iodine: Bernard Courtois. Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.

This long-term skin condition occurs when dead skin cells and oil clog hair follicles, producing blackheads, whiteheads, and pimples mainly on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne is a long-term skin condition that occurs when dead skin cells and sebum clog hair follicles.
This Indian economist won the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his work on welfare economics and has also studied the causes of famines — who is he?
Amartya Sen (born 3 November 1933) is an Indian economist and philosopher.
What term describes the discipline of measuring human body dimensions, applied everywhere from ergonomics and architecture to tracking historical living standards?
Anthropometry (from Ancient Greek (nthrpos) 'human' and (mtron) 'measure') refers to the measurement of the human individual.
This common long-term inflammatory airway disease causes wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath that can flare into sudden attacks triggered by allergens or pollen. What condition is it?
Asthma is a common long-term inflammatory disease of the airways. It is characterized by variable and recurring symptoms and reduced lung function.
A civil-engineering graduate who first reshaped his father's firm toward real estate, this Frenchman now chairs the world's largest luxury goods company — who is he?
Bernard Arnault (born 5 March 1949) is a French businessman.
Every subatomic particle is either this integer-spin class or a fermion; Paul Dirac named the class after physicist Satyendra Nath Bose, whose statistics they obey — what's the class called?
Boson is a subatomic particle whose spin quantum number has an integer value (0, 1, 2,...).
Produced when quicklime is mixed with water, this white, powdery compound goes by many names in industry and food prep, where it's labeled E526 — what compound is it?
Calcium hydroxide (traditionally called slaked lime) is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula Ca(OH)2.
Retired from Istanbul Technical University, this geologist holds foreign membership in both the US and Russian National Academies of Sciences. Who is he?
Celâl Şengör (born 24 March 1955) is a Turkish geologist.

This genus of flowering trees and shrubs, native to South and East Asia, Melanesia, and Australia, gave rise through extensive hybridization to oranges, lemons, grapefruits, and limes — what's the genus called?
Citrus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs in the family Rutaceae.

What zoological term describes the internal-fertilization mating behavior in which a male animal introduces sperm directly into a female's reproductive tract — occurring via a 'cloacal kiss' in birds and most reptiles, or vaginally in mammals?
Copulation (zoology) is animal sexual behavior in which a male introduces sperm into the female's body, especially directly into the female's reproductive tract.
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded a company later acquired by MSC Software in 1998, then went on to co-found and lead a massively popular online gaming and creation platform — who is he?
David Baszucki (buh-; born January 20, 1963) is a Canadian-born American entrepreneur, engineer, and software developer.
This Penn professor's discoveries about modified nucleosides made the Pfizer and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines possible, earning him a share of the 2023 Nobel Prize in Medicine — who is he?
Drew Weissman (born September 7, 1959) is an American physician and immunologist known for his contributions to RNA biology.
This branch of medicine studies the body's hormone-secreting glands and the chemical messengers, called hormones, that regulate growth, metabolism, mood, and more — name the field?
Endocrinology (from endocrine + -ology) is a branch of biology and medicine dealing with the endocrine system, its diseases, and its specific secretions known as hormones.
Known for filling pillows and blankets as well as lining the wings of birds, what are these soft, complex integumentary structures called?
Feather are epidermal growths that form a distinctive outer covering, or plumage, on both avian (bird) and some non-avian dinosaurs and other archosaurs.

This American mechanical engineer and pioneering management consultant wrote a 1909 book that Academy of Management fellows later voted the most influential management book of the entire 20th century — who was he?
Frederick Winslow Taylor (March 20, 1856 - March 21, 1915) was an American mechanical engineer.

Encoded by the codons CAA and CAG and structurally related to glutamic acid but with an amide in place of a carboxylic acid group, this charge-neutral amino acid becomes essential under bodily stress — which amino acid?
Glutamine (symbol Gln or Q) is an -amino acid that is used in the biosynthesis of proteins.

This herbivorous mammal, the largest in its family of lagomorphs, nests in shallow ground depressions called 'forms' and is built for speed with long hind legs and heat-dissipating ears — what animal is it?
Hare are mammals belonging to the genus Lepus.
Which cosmological relationship says a galaxy's recession speed is proportional to its distance from Earth, discovered via redshift measurements and usually credited to a 1929 paper?
Hubble's law is the observation in physical cosmology that galaxies are moving away from Earth at speeds proportional to their distance.
This post-transition metal, chemically similar to gallium and thallium, was identified spectroscopically in 1863 and takes its name from the indigo line in its spectrum — what element is it?
Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
Enlisting as a valet named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist disguised herself as a man and became the first woman to sail all the way around the globe — who was she?

Jeanne Baret (27 July 1740 - 5 August 1807) was a French explorer, naturalist, and botanist who is recognised as the first woman to have completed a voyage of circumnavigation of the globe, which she did via boat.
Native to eastern and southern Africa, this flowering shrub is the sole species in its genus and has a documented history of cultivation dating back to Ethiopia's Harar region. Name the plant?
Khat (Catha edulis), also known as Bushman's tea, especially in South Africa, is a species of flowering plant in the family Celastraceae, and the sole species in genus Catha.
This bacterial blood infection, spread between humans, dogs, and rodents, can range from symptomless to a severe form that turns skin and eyes yellow and shuts down the kidneys — what disease is it?
Leptospirosis is a blood infection caused by bacteria of the genus Leptospira that can infect humans, dogs, rodents, and many other wild and domesticated animals.
Born in Vienna into one of Europe's richest families, this philosopher studied under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge and transformed 20th-century philosophy of language and logic — who is he?

Ludwig Wittgenstein ((h)tyne; Austrian; 26 April 1889 - 29 April 1951) was an Austro-British philosopher who worked in logic, philosophy of mathematics, philosophy of mind, and philosophy of language.
The heaviest and largest members of the squirrel family, these 15 species of grazing ground-dwellers vanish each winter to hibernate underground — what are they?
Marmot are large ground squirrels in the genus Marmota, with 15 species living in Asia, Europe, and North America.
This Cuban engineer-turned-politician became his country's top leader in 2021, making him the first head of Cuba since the 1959 revolution who isn't a member of the Castro family — who is he?

Miguel Díaz-Canel (Latin American; born 20 April 1960) is a Cuban politician and engineer who has served as the 8th First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba and the top leader of Cuba since 2021.

Chemically known as bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide, this organosulfur compound is a potent alkylating agent and carcinogen with no preventive antidote — protection relies entirely on covering the skin and airways. Name this notorious chemical warfare agent?
Mustard gas are names commonly used for the organosulfur chemical compound bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide, which has the chemical structure S(CH2CH2Cl)2, as well as other species.
Catalyzed in nature by iron-bearing nitrogenase enzymes and famously partnered with legumes, this process turns molecular N2 into ammonia — what's it called?
Nitrogen fixation is a chemical process by which molecular dinitrogen (N2) is converted into ammonia (NH3).
This systemic skeletal disorder develops when the rate of bone breakdown outpaces new bone formation with age, leaving bones porous, less dense, and prone to fracture — what's the condition called?
Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disorder characterized by low bone mass, micro-architectural deterioration of bone tissue leading to more porous bone, and consequent increase in fracture risk.
Innervated by two dedicated nerves and inserting near the upper arm's bicipital groove, which broad chest muscle flexes and internally rotates the humerus?
Pectoralis major (from Latin pectus 'breast') is a thick, fan-shaped or triangular convergent muscle of the human chest.

This eating disorder involves compulsively craving or eating substances not meant for consumption, and takes its name from the Latin word for a magpie famed in folklore for eating anything — what is it?
Pica (disorder) is the psychologically compulsive craving or consumption of objects that are not normally intended to be consumed.
Which compound pulls double duty as a dietary iodine supplement and as the pill that protects the thyroid gland during radiation emergencies?
Potassium iodide (KI) is a chemical compound, medication, and dietary supplement.
This collective name covers several genera of mid-sized game birds, split between Old World and New World families despite their similar appearance — what birds are they?
Quail is a collective name for several genera of mid-sized birds generally placed in the order Galliformes.
With a surface temperature over 12,000 Kelvin and a radius more than seventy times the Sun's, this blue supergiant is the brightest point of light in Orion — which star?
Rigel is a blue supergiant star in the equatorial constellation of Orion.
Milder than most of its Allium relatives like garlic and leeks, this vegetable has a long, hollow green stem and no fully developed bulb — what is it commonly called?
Scallion (also known as green onions and spring onions) are edible vegetables of various species in the genus Allium.
Set in Miami, this NBC sitcom follows four older women sharing a home as they navigate friendship, aging, and daily life, led by Bea Arthur and Betty White. What show is it?
Silicone is a polymer composed of repeating units of siloxane (OSiR2OSiR2, where "R" stands for an organic group).
Members of the family Sciuridae, whose closest living relatives are surprisingly the mountain beaver and dormice, these rodents are native to the Americas, Eurasia and Africa — what are they called?
Squirrel (z)) are members of the family Sciuridae (sih-, -dee), a family that includes small or medium-sized rodents.
Serving as prime minister seven separate times before becoming president from 1993 to 2000, this Turkish statesman led two different political parties across his long career — who was he?
Süleyman Demirel (1 November 1924 - 17 June 2015) was a Turkish politician, engineer, and statesman who served as the president of Turkey from 1993 to 2000.

When a piece of this obstruction breaks free and travels through the body it's called an embolus, and it can trigger a stroke or heart attack — what is the formation of a blood clot inside a vessel called?
Thrombosis (from Ancient Greek (thrmbsis) 'clotting') is the formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel, obstructing the flow of blood through the circulatory system.
These large, heavyset American game birds have a distinctive fleshy growth called a snood hanging from the base of their beak, with wild and ocellated species. What birds are they?
Turkey (bird) are large, heavyset galliforms in the genus Meleagris, indigenous to the Americas.
An American investor and philanthropist, he is the chairman of Berkshire Hathaway and, as of January 2026, the ninth-richest person in the world. Who is he?
Warren Buffett (born August 30, 1930) is an American investor and philanthropist who is the chairman and former CEO of the conglomerate Berkshire Hathaway.
Also known as AZT, this was the very first antiretroviral drug used against HIV/AIDS, and can be given during birth to prevent mother-to-child spread — what is it?
Zidovudine (ZDV), also known as azidothymidine (AZT), was the first antiretroviral medication used to prevent and treat HIV/AIDS.
Nicknamed the cell's "molecular unit of currency," this energy-carrying molecule powers muscle contraction and nerve impulses, dropping to ADP or AMP when spent — what is it?
Adenosine triphosphate: Energy-carrying molecule in living cells.
This French surgeon won a 1912 Nobel for pioneering blood-vessel suturing and later teamed with aviator Charles Lindbergh to build an early perfusion pump for organ work. Who was he?
Alexis Carrel: French surgeon and biologist (1873–1944)
Domesticated in Southwest China roughly 2,000 years ago, this corm-producing plant is nicknamed 'devil's tongue' and gets boiled down into a jelly-like noodle called shirataki — what is it?
Amorphophallus konjac: Edible plant from Yunnan, China.
Central to the 18th-century chemical revolution, this French nobleman named oxygen in 1778 and overturned the phlogiston theory of combustion — who is he?
Antoine Lavoisier: French nobleman and chemist (1743–1794)
Dubbed the 'Prophet of the Space Age,' this English science fiction author co-wrote the screenplay for 2001: A Space Odyssey and formed sci-fi's 'Big Three' with Heinlein and Asimov — who is he?

Brine: Concentrated solution of salt in water.

Calendula: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.

Carpenter bee: Common name for a genus of bees.

Citric acid cycle: Interconnected biochemical reactions releasing energy.

Coma: State of unconsciousness. The person may experience respiratory and circulatory problems due to the body's inability to maintain normal bodily functions.
First described in 1880 by a French neurologist, this rare delusion convinces sufferers that they are dead, don't exist, or have lost their internal organs — what is it called?
Cotard's syndrome: Delusion that one is dead or non-existent.

Dung beetle: Informal group of insects.

Elm: Flowering, deciduous trees, family Ulmaceae.

Ether: Organic compounds made of alkyl/aryl groups bound to oxygen (R–O–R')
Known for its smooth silvery-grey bark and toxin-laced but edible nuts, this deciduous tree native to Europe includes the striking copper-leaved cultivar among its ornamentals — which species?
Fagus sylvatica: Species of deciduous tree. It is native to much of Europe, growing in humid climates.
This normal, occasionally embarrassing bodily process brings intestinal gas to the rectum, pressurizes it with muscle contractions, and releases it through the anus — what is it?
Flatulence: Bodily function of expelling intestinal gas from the anus.
Known as the brain's chief inhibitory neurotransmitter, this compound is also sold as a dietary supplement despite debate over whether it crosses the blood-brain barrier — what is it?
GABA: Main inhibitory neurotransmitter in the mammalian brain.
The longest member of the weasel family at up to 1.8 meters, this noisy, highly social river-dweller lives in family groups along the Amazon and in the Pantanal — which animal?

Great egret: Species of bird. The great egret (Ardea alba), also known as the common egret, large egret, great white egret, or great white heron, is a large, widely distributed egret.

Hare: Genus of mammals in the family Leporidae.
This seasonal state of drastically reduced metabolism, breathing, and heart rate lets animals conserve energy through winter months, with 'aestivation' as its summer counterpart — what is it called?
Hibernation: Physiological state of dormant inactivity in order to pass the winter season.

Indian peafowl: Species of bird. The Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), also known as the common peafowl, or blue peafowl, is a species of peafowl native to the Indian subcontinent.

John von Neumann: Hungarian and American mathematician and physicist (1903–1957)

Kitty O'Neil: American stuntwoman and racer (1946–2018)

Legionnaires' disease: Form of atypical pneumonia. Legionnaires' disease is a form of atypical pneumonia caused by any species of Legionella bacteria, quite often Legionella pneumophila.
Named after both a biblical sea monster and the author of 'Moby-Dick,' this extinct predatory sperm whale roamed ancient oceans roughly 9 million years ago — which genus?
Livyatan: Extinct genus of sperm whale from the Miocene epoch.
Native to northeastern Australia and first commercially grown at scale in Hawaii during the 1880s, this is the only widely cultivated food plant indigenous to Australia — what nut is it?
Macadamia: Genus of plants indigenous to Australia.
The heaviest members of the squirrel family, these ground-dwelling herbivores live in groups through the summer before disappearing underground to hibernate all winter — what are they?

This WWII German monoplane fighter formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe alongside the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, though Allied aircrew nicknamed it after its designer — which aircraft?

Produced by mammary glands and rich in calcium, protein and lactose, this liquid is often prized for its antibody-packed early form, colostrum — what is it?
Milk: Nutrient-rich liquid produced by mammals.
Grown above the upper lip and below the nose, this facial hair style has taken many forms across history — what is it called?
Moustache: Strip of facial hair across the upper lip. A moustache (UK:) or mustache (US:) is a growth of facial hair grown above the upper lip and under the nose of men.

Neck: Body part that connects the head and torso. It supports the weight of the head and protects the nerves that transmit sensory and motor information between the brain and the rest of the body.

Flown by William J. Knight to a record 4,520 mph in 1967 — a mark that still stands — this rocket-powered aircraft was part of an experimental series operated by the Air Force and NASA — which aircraft?
North American X-15: Rocket-powered aircraft and spaceplane operated by the US Air Force and NASA.
The most arboreal of the great apes, with long arms, short legs and reddish-brown hair, this genus Pongo primate survives today only in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra — what is it?
Orangutan: Genus of Asian apes. The most arboreal of the great apes, orangutans spend most of their time in trees.

This nerve-damage condition can be triggered by diabetes, vitamin B12 deficiency, or certain chemotherapy and antibiotic drugs, and may come on suddenly or creep in slowly — what is it?
Peripheral neuropathy: Nervous system disease affecting nerves beyond the brain and spinal cord.
Boasting the longest cones of any spruce and widely planted as a Christmas tree, this European conifer was also the first gymnosperm to have its genome sequenced — which species?
Picea abies: Species of plant. Picea abies, the Norway spruce, Norway fir or European spruce, is a species of spruce native to Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.
Nicknamed the 'terror of Bengal' for choking waterways across the world, this South American aquatic plant is commonly known as water hyacinth — what is its scientific name?
Pontederia crassipes: Aquatic plant native to the Amazon basin.

Marketed under brand names like Sudafed, this nasal decongestant can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant at higher doses, making it both a medicine-cabinet staple and, at times, a drug of abuse. What is it?
Pseudoephedrine: Synthetic decongestant. Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
Nicknamed the 'stinking corpse lily,' this Southeast Asian plant genus produces the world's largest flower and was first seen by a Briton in 1818 after a local servant pointed it out — which genus?
Made up of 12 paired bones plus the sternum and spine, this bony enclosure of the chest shields the heart and lungs while housing the muscles used for breathing — what is it?
Rib cage: Bone structure of the thorax.
Originally conceived as a jet trainer before its role expanded to supersonic strike and reconnaissance, this Anglo-French attack aircraft is today flown only by the Indian Air Force. What is it?
SEPECAT Jaguar: French/British attack aircraft. It was also later license produced by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited in India for use of the Indian Air Force.
Located at the base of the penis in most male mammals, this sac of skin holding the testicles tends to tighten when exposed to cold — what is it called?
Scrotum: Sac of skin that protects the testicles.
Named for a Swedish medical physicist, this SI unit measures the stochastic health risk of ionizing radiation, such as equivalent and effective dose — what unit is it?
Sievert: Derived SI unit of equivalent dose of ionizing radiation. One sievert equals 100 rem, which is an older, CGS radiation unit.
Also nicknamed 'sour dock,' this perennial herb native to Eurasia is often eaten as a tangy leaf vegetable in grassland habitats — which plant?
Sorrel: Flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae.
Sitting between the esophagus and the small intestine, this muscular organ uses acid and enzymes to chemically break down food, giving us the word 'gastric' — which organ?
Stomach: Digestive organ. The stomach is a muscular, hollow organ in the upper gastrointestinal tract of humans and many other animals, including several invertebrates.
Sold under the brand name Cialis, this erectile dysfunction medication can remain effective for up to 36 hours after a single dose — which drug?
Tadalafil: Medication used to treat erectile dysfunction.
Native to the tropical Americas, this small evergreen tree's fermented seeds become cocoa powder, cocoa butter, and chocolate — which tree?
Theobroma cacao: Species of tree grown for its seeds.
Located at either side of the back of your throat, these paired lymphoid organs form part of a defensive ring guarding the entrance to your digestive and respiratory tracts — what are they?

Tonsil: Lymphoid organs in the mouth and throat. The palatine tonsils and the adenoid tonsil are organs consisting of lymphoepithelial tissue located near the oropharynx and nasopharynx (parts of the throat).
Renowned as the greatest astronomer before the invention of the telescope, this Dane noticed an unexpectedly bright new star in 1572 and devoted himself to ever more precise instruments. Who was he?

Comprising some 150 to 175 species of shrubs and the occasional small tree, this flowering-plant genus is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere but in Africa survives only in the Atlas Mountains — which genus?

Geely Auto: People's Republic of China. It owns the eponymous Geely Auto brand and partly owns Lynk & Co, Proton Cars and Zeekr brands.
In which country is Geely based?
Geely: People's Republic of China. The company was founded by, and is privately owned by Chinese entrepreneur Li Shufu.

Founded in 1990 by Mikhail Fridman, this Moscow-headquartered private lender is Russia's largest of its kind, though its founder left the board in 2022 after EU sanctions over the invasion of Ukraine — which institution?
Alfa-Bank is the largest of the private banks in Russia. It was founded in 1990 by Russian businessman Mikhail Fridman, who remains the controlling owner.
Founded in Rome in 1925 by two fashion designers, which Italian luxury house — known for its fur and leather goods — has been part of LVMH's Fashion & Leather Goods division since 2001?
Fendi (Italian) is an Italian luxury fashion house producing fur, ready-to-wear, leather goods, shoes, fragrances, eyewear, timepieces and accessories.
The one-time chief designer and vice-president of his family's famous Italian fashion house, this businessman is credited with helping create its iconic double-G logo — who was he?
Paolo Gucci (29 March 1931 - 10 October 1995) was an Italian businessman and fashion designer.
Over 90% owned by Russian state agencies, this financial institution formerly known as Vneshtorgbank operates a subsidiary branch in Shanghai — which institution is it?
VTB Bank (formerly known as Vneshtorgbank) is a Russian majority state-owned bank headquartered in Moscow.
After resigning from the New York Times with a widely publicized public letter, this journalist founded The Free Press and now serves as editor-in-chief of CBS News — who is she?
Bari Weiss: American journalist and political commentator (born 1984)

Founded in Annecy, France, in 2009 and later acquired by Deckers Brands, this running-shoe company pioneered oversized 'maximalist' midsoles — which brand?
Hoka: Athletic shoe company from France.

Headquartered in Budapest and flying a fleet exclusively from one European planemaker, this Hungarian ultra-low-cost carrier trails only Ryanair and easyJet in size across Europe — which carrier?
